title: The Pharmacy
strapline: Prescription in, medicine out — counting the tablets, reading the label, and always checking with a grown-up first.
intent: The pharmacist is a community helper who keeps us well, and playing out a pharmacy helps children understand a familiar place while learning, crucially, that real medicine is only ever handled by grown-ups.
The role play builds knowledge of the people and places that help us stay healthy and get better when we are unwell.
Counting out 'medicines', reading labels, measuring spoonfuls and matching prescriptions is purposeful mathematics and early literacy.
Serving customers, taking prescriptions and giving careful instructions grows real conversation and clear communication.
The vital safety message — that medicine is never a treat, and only a trusted grown-up gives it — is woven in gently and memorably through the play.
Real vocabulary and knowledge grow — pharmacy, medicine, prescription, label, dose, healthy, careful, chemist.
implementation: Set up a pharmacy — a counter, a till, empty (clean) boxes and bottles, pretend tablets (counters or beads), a prescription pad, labels and a set of shelves.
Take a customer's role so children fill prescriptions, count out doses and advise: 'The doctor says two spoonfuls a day — can you measure that out and write it on the label?'
Model the careful, informative talk and, warmly but clearly, the safety rule: 'Real medicine is never a sweet — only a grown-up you trust ever gives it to you.'
Bring in maths and literacy through the play — count and measure the doses, read and write labels, match the prescription to the medicine, handle money.
Add prescription slips, labels and a reminder chart for real reading and writing, and organise the shelves in an order children design.
Link it to real knowledge — how the pharmacy helps the doctor and the community keep us well — and always keep every prop plainly pretend.
key_questions: The doctor says two spoonfuls a day — can you measure that and write it on the label?
How many tablets does this prescription need?
Who is the only person who ever gives you real medicine?
Can you match this prescription to the right box?
How shall we organise the shelves so we can find things?
